title: What do movies about power, corruption and crime like Citizen Kane tell us about the world leaders nowadays?

commenti.body:
That some things never ever change. While technology may shift, or giant leaps in medicine many films.

Metropolis for instance shows how power operates the same way it does now as it did then. The working class held down by dynastically rich families that continue to stay rich.

This goes for history in general which I’ve been reading is we see this cycle over and over again. But what is refreshing are the stories that show that people hit a breaking point and inevitably break free against seeimingly unstoppable forces of power.

Like the French Revolution. Average citizens, starving weak and poor grabbed torches and pitchforks and overthrew an armed government and ended dynastic rule.

A big part of Cormac McCarthy’s writing orbits around the theme that regardless of scientific and economic advancement we have still not improved as a species. The human parts of our species that seek to destroy each other are exactly the same as they were a thousand years ago, the only things that change are the tools and methods. Our tendency to be inspired by the wrong people (Kane, Gatsby, Judge Holden, Tyler Durden, Tony Soprano) and prioritize the wrong things (material gains, influence over others, disposition to violence) hold us back era after era.

People like William Randolph Hearst (the inspiration for Charles Kane) always go to great lengths to show how happy they are in flaunting their wealth. The real Hearst was incensed that Citizen Kane showed him as a bitter old failure, and tried to limit showings of the film. I’ve also read accounts from members the Hearst family that say something like, oh grandpa was nothing like the movie, he loved life and his possessions, etc. But from what we can see with contemporaries in this mold, like Trump and Musk, is that their love of being the center of attention is stronger than their good sense and business acumen. There has to be a deep hollow in someone’s life to want to do that.

There's a very short interview Errol Morris did with Donald Trump about why he loves Citizen Kane so much. Watching it with this in mind is eye opening. He really seems to have modeled himself off the most rotten parts of Charles Foster Kane. Making of fake news, sewing doubt in elections, cozying up to fascists when he feels like it, the cocky bravura – all borrowed from Charles Foster Kane. The difference is that Kane had a shred of decency to lose and a the elequense befitting a tragic figure. If Trump has either, he's hidden it expertly.
